documents.title: Software update notice: TaskFlow version 5.2
documents.text:
Version 5.2 of TaskFlow will be released on Tuesday 9 June between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. (Eastern Time), during which the service will be unavailable. We recommend that you save your work and log out by midnight on Monday.

What is new: a redesigned calendar view that shows deadlines from several projects in a single screen; the option to assign one task to multiple people; and a faster search tool that also looks inside attached files. The mobile application has been updated to support these features and should be installed through your usual app store once the release is complete.

What is changing: the old "Reports" menu has been merged into "Insights," and some saved reports may appear under new names. Reports will not be lost, but you may need to recreate any filters that used custom fields. Integration with the Calibre calendar tool will end on 30 June; customers who rely on it should switch to the standard calendar export described in our help center.

If you encounter problems after the update, please contact support through the in-app chat, which is available around the clock, rather than by e-mail, where replies may take up to two days. Administrators can find a detailed list of changes in the release notes.

questions.explanation: The notice announces version 5.2, describing new features, changes and downtime.

documents.title: Request for catering quotation
documents.text:
To: Seaview Catering
From: Beatriz Moreno, Events Coordinator, Altura Biotech
Subject: Quotation for annual partners' dinner

Dear Seaview Catering,

We are organizing our annual partners' dinner on Saturday 18 October at the Harbour Pavilion and would like a quotation for approximately 120 guests. We would like a three-course menu with a vegetarian option and at least two dishes that are free of gluten. Service should begin at 7:30 p.m., and the venue will be available for setup from 3 p.m. We would also appreciate a recommendation for non-alcoholic drinks, since several guests do not drink alcohol. Our budget is around 55 dollars per person, including service.

Could you let us know by 15 September whether you are available and what you would propose?

Kind regards,
Beatriz Moreno

documents.title: Quotation: Altura Biotech partners' dinner
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Moreno,

Thank you for thinking of Seaview Catering. We are available on 18 October and would be delighted to cater your dinner. Our proposal is a three-course menu: a roasted pumpkin soup or smoked trout to begin, a main course of herb-crusted lamb, sea bass or a mushroom and chestnut wellington, and a choice of two desserts. Both the soup and the sea bass are gluten-free, and the wellington is vegetarian.

The price is 58 dollars per person for the set menu, including service, plus 9 dollars per person for a package of non-alcoholic cocktails and juices. Because the Pavilion's kitchen is small, we would need to bring our own equipment, which carries a flat charge of 600 dollars. A deposit of 30 percent is required to confirm the booking.

If you would like to adjust the price, we could replace the lamb with a chicken dish, which would reduce the cost by 4 dollars per person.

Sincerely,
Luca Ferraro, Seaview Catering

documents.title: Re: Quotation
documents.text:
Dear Mr. Ferraro,

Thank you for the proposal. We would like to proceed with the chicken option and the non-alcoholic package, but the guest list is now 110 rather than 120. Could you confirm the new total and send the details of the deposit? Please also note that setup will now begin at 2 p.m., since the venue has asked us to vacate by 11 p.m. instead of midnight.

Regards,
Beatriz Moreno

documents.title: Ridgeway Outdoor Supplies: Return policy
documents.text:
We want you to be satisfied with every purchase. Most items may be returned within 45 days of delivery for a full refund, provided they are unused and in their original packaging. Footwear may be tried indoors, but shoes showing signs of outdoor wear cannot be accepted. Tents and sleeping bags must be returned unwashed and free of odors; items that have been used for camping are not eligible for a refund but may be considered for repair under our warranty.

To return an item, log in to your account and print the prepaid label. Refunds are made to the original payment method within seven working days of receiving the parcel. Return shipping is free for orders over 100 dollars; for smaller orders a fee of 6 dollars is deducted from the refund. Custom-engraved products and clearance items marked 'final sale' cannot be returned.

documents.title: Problem with my order #44-3190
documents.text:
Dear Ridgeway,

I received my hiking boots, size 43, three weeks ago. After wearing them indoors for a few days, I realize that they are too narrow. Unfortunately, I also wore them for a short walk to the post office, and they have some mud on the soles. The order total was 94 dollars. I would like to return them, or exchange them for the wide version if you have it.

Thank you,
Evelyn Cho

documents.title: Ridgeway live chat
documents.text:
Customer service (Joel): Hello, Ms. Cho. I've read your message. Unfortunately, because the boots have been worn outdoors, we cannot offer a refund. However, I can offer something for you. We have the wide version in size 43 in stock. If you send the narrow pair back, I can arrange an exchange at a 20 percent discount on the wide pair as a courtesy, given that the walk was brief.
Evelyn Cho: That's generous. Will I need to pay for shipping?
Customer service (Joel): Since this is an exchange rather than a return for refund, the label will be free of charge. I'll e-mail it now. The new boots will be sent when we receive the old ones, which usually takes four to five days.

documents.title: Letter of recommendation
documents.text:
To whom it may concern,

I am pleased to recommend Ayesha Karim for the position of Production Supervisor at your Dunmore facility. I have been Ms. Karim's manager at Westfield Packaging for six years, during which she rose from machine operator to shift leader, and I can say without hesitation that she is one of the most dependable people I have supervised.

Ms. Karim's greatest strength is her ability to remain calm when schedules are disrupted. Last winter, when a supplier delivered the wrong materials during our busiest month, she reorganized the line within hours and avoided any delay to our customers. She also took the initiative to introduce a weekly briefing in which operators identify safety hazards, and the number of minor accidents in her unit has fallen by a third as a result.

If I have one reservation, it is that Ms. Karim sometimes hesitates to delegate, preferring to check details herself. She is aware of this and has recently completed a course in team leadership. I believe a role with a larger team will help her develop further. We will be sorry to lose her, but she deserves the opportunity.

Sincerely,
Thomas Berg, Operations Manager

documents.title: Production Supervisor, Dunmore
documents.text: Hartley Foods seeks a Production Supervisor to manage a team of 25 operators on rotating shifts. The ideal candidate has five years of experience in a manufacturing environment, including two in a leadership role, and a proven record in health and safety. The supervisor will be responsible for scheduling, monitoring output and handling disputes. Applicants should be able to demonstrate how they have improved efficiency or reduced incidents. Applications close on 3 November, and interviews will take place in the week of 17 November at the Dunmore facility. Candidates will be asked to describe a situation in which they had to manage a conflict within a team, and to explain what they learned from it. The company offers a relocation allowance, a pension plan and thirty days of paid annual leave.

documents.title: Cycling commuters set to gain a new route
documents.text:
The city council has approved funding for a two-kilometer protected cycle path along Ferris Road, one of the busiest arteries in the northern suburbs. Construction is due to start in March and will be completed by September, provided the winter is not unusually harsh. The path will be separated from motor traffic by a raised curb and will include dedicated signals at five intersections.

The project has drawn support from a coalition of employers, including the hospital and two large insurance firms, who argue that safer cycling will ease parking pressure on their sites. Opponents, mainly shop owners along the road, fear that the loss of twenty-six on-street parking spaces will harm trade. The council has responded by promising a review after twelve months and by offering to extend deliveries hours for affected businesses.

Transport officer Mina Haddad says that a trial last year, in which a temporary lane was marked with paint, increased the number of cyclists by forty percent. She concedes, however, that the figure was recorded in summer and that numbers might be lower during winter months. "We are not trying to force anyone out of their car," she says. "We are trying to make the alternative more attractive."

questions.explanation: A coalition of employers including the hospital and two insurance firms support it; shop owners oppose it.

questions.explanation: They fear the loss of twenty-six parking spaces will harm trade.

questions.explanation: The project has gained the support of a group of employers, so it has 'attracted backing'.
